text:
Michael Bunting wasn't on a roster when the season started. Philadelphia signed him to a one-year deal on Oct 6, after the Flyers opened without a win, and he scored his first goal for them in Vancouver on Nov 9. Not everyone is sold: Broad Street Hockey argued on Saturday that the Flyers "are making a mistake by playing Michael Bunting over Cole Knuble".

Eleven games is a small sample, and so far it isn't pretty. He has 2 points on about 11 minutes a night, and at five on five the Flyers have had just 36.5% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, 7 points worse than without him. Some of it is finishing: 1 goal on 1.65 expected, shooting 6%. The case for patience is last season. Evolving-Hockey had him worth 1.4 wins above replacement, in the 88th percentile among forwards at driving play, and +2.8 goals from drawing more penalties than he takes. That player hasn't shown up in Philadelphia yet, and until he does, the Knuble debate isn't going away.
headline: Bunting has a goal, a role and a debate
